gap: No result ChatGPT got states what it costs to remove the AI bird-ID subscription: on the makers' own stores, Kiwibit charges $40 once for lifetime AI on its 4K solar feeder ($139.99 vs $179.99), while Birdfy charges $60 for one year of Plus on every solar feeder it bundles ($199.99 vs $259.99 for the Metal 2 4K, for example).
standout_why: I compared against reviewed.com (Nov 6), birdfeederlab.com (Aug 22) and the four ChatGPT cards. Reviewed.com lists recurring rates only: $79.99/yr ($39.99 on sale) for Birdfy 2 Pro, $98.99/yr for Birdbuddy Home auto ID, $4.49/mo for Kiwibit 2. For Kiwibit lifetime AI it gives no price ('lifetime AI available'). Birdfeederlab says it gives no subscription prices at all. Neither page puts a one-time price on lifetime AI or totals first-year and later-year cost from same-day maker prices. The cited WIRED and Good Housekeeping pages blocked fetching (WebFetch refused both domains), so I could not check them, and the gap is only provisional against them. ChatGPT's cards also show retailer prices above what the makers charge today: Birdfy Wood $149.99 at Chewy vs $119.99 at birdfy.com, and Kiwibit 4K $159.99 at Chewy vs $139.99 at kiwibit.com.
decides: For a shopper who taps 'No monthly subscription': the Kiwibit 4K Solar Panel Kit with Lifetime AI ($179.99, 3 W panel, 5,200 mAh) has the lowest cost with no recurring AI fee among the models I priced. Birdfy Metal A + 1 year Plus ($169.99) is cheaper in year one but renews. Birdbuddy Pro Solar ($199.99 at Target) costs the most up front, and per Target's Q&A, Premium unlocks its '2K Ultra Resolution'. If AI ID doesn't matter, Birdfy Feeder with Solar Panel 2K and Feeder Wood at $119.99 on birdfy.com are the cheapest solar 2K options, $30 under the Chewy price ChatGPT showed for the Wood.
